_about: What each QuillVille app requires, declared in one place a build can read.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The shared runtime is the union of every app's Python
dependencies -- quillville-runtime.spec says so in as many words -- and that
union is dominated by the editor. Measured on the 2026-08-19 build, 110.1 MB
of the 284.1 MB Python payload (38.8%) is the documents stack and the spell
checker, and the editor is the only thing that can call either. Eight apps
install it anyway.
Splitting those into loadable layers (Stage 3 of the runtime layering plan)
is real engineering and is not started. This file is its prerequisite and is
useful on its own: it is the first place that says, in a form a test can
check, which app needs what. REQUIRED_COMPONENTS in each app module already
declares external tools; nothing declared Python layers, so nothing could
notice that Quill Weather ships a PDF renderer.
WHAT IS ENFORCED TODAY. tests/unit/structure/test_app_profiles.py checks that
every shipped entry point has a row here, that every row names a module that
exists, and that each row's `components` matches that module's own
REQUIRED_COMPONENTS exactly -- so the build-side declaration and the runtime
one cannot drift. `layers` is declaration only: no loader reads it yet.
WHAT IS NOT ENFORCED YET. Nothing checks a built artifact against the layer
membership below. scripts/runtime_layer_report.py measures and reports it;
making that a gate is Stage 4.

why: Reading, converting and describing documents. Every member was traced to
an import under quill/io, quill/core/math, quill/core/ai/vision.py or
quill/platform/windows -- surfaces that exist only in the editor. The
standalone apps open their bundled help as pre-rendered HTML through the
system browser (app_shell.open_app_document), so none of them reaches

Names are spelled as scripts/check_runtime_inventory.py's normalize() produces them, so the report and the inventory gate cannot disagree about what a top-level entry is. A trailing * matches by prefix, for the two DLLs PyInstaller renames with a content hash.
pyenchant plus the pruned libenchant payload. Only quill/core/spellcheck.py
and quill/core/spell_languages.py import it, and only the editor reaches
those -- the fact that changed the whole language plan in the 2026-08-18
retrospective, where it had looked like a cost shared across eight apps.
QUILL Social has a spell-check keymap entry and a PRD section and no code;
when that is built, Social joins this layer and not before.

quill.name: QUILL
notes: The editor. The app the union was sized for, so layering saves it
nothing -- which is the point: everyone else is paying for this row.
Declares no REQUIRED_COMPONENTS today even though speech export uses
ffmpeg; that is a real gap, listed with the others below.

radio.name: Quill Radio
notes: ffmpeg records; libmpv is the playback engine that delivers DVR, output
device routing, Volume Boost, native Sound Enhancements, stream track
titles, stall detection and Ogg/Opus/HLS. Both are staged into the
shared runtime's tools/ by its own build_release.ps1.

cast.name: QUILL Cast
notes: Stages ffmpeg only -- 110 MB of libmpv it has no use for.

studio.name: QUILL Audio Studio
notes: The declaration was corrected to match the build after the 2026-08-17
layering work found it declaring ffmpeg only while staging libmpv too.

weather.name: Quill Weather
notes: The leanest app, and the one layering would help most.

inkwell.name: Quill Inkwell
notes: Text expansion. No media, no documents.

converter.name: Quill Converter
notes: UNDECLARED MEDIA USE. converter.py calls find_ffmpeg() and passes the
result to available_output_formats(), which returns exactly ["wav"]
when ffmpeg is absent -- an audio converter that can only write WAV.
It declares no components and its build_release.ps1 does not call
Stage-QuillMediaTools, so nothing installs or refcounts ffmpeg for it.
Left as a finding rather than a change: adding ffmpeg here is a
packaging decision, not a refactor.

player.name: Quill Media Player
notes: UNDECLARED MEDIA USE. Announces "Audio effects need the libmpv engine"
and reports which backend it is on, so it knows about libmpv and
declares nothing. Same finding shape as Converter.

beacon.name: Quill Beacon
notes: UNDECLARED MEDIA USE, mildest of the three: beacon/player.py documents
an opt-in libmpv backend and falls back to wx.media, so the absence
degrades rather than breaks.

social.name: QUILL Social
notes: Ships as its own wheel (quill_social), vendored in vendor/wheels and
collected into the shared runtime; there is no quill/apps module for it, so
`entry` is null and the profile test skips the REQUIRED_COMPONENTS check.
Will join the spellcheck layer if and when its specified-but-unbuilt spell
check is written -- it has a keymap entry and a PRD section and no code.
